proposal.summary: Improper input validation in the CLI of Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows an authenticated remote attacker with Administrator credentials to inject OS commands into a legitimate command, escape the restricted command prompt, and execute arbitrary commands on the underlying OS.

AC.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by injecting operating system commands into a legitimate command.

PR.quote: To successfully exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would need valid Administrator credentials.

UI.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by injecting operating system commands into a legitimate command.

S.quote: A successful exploit could allow the attacker to escape the restricted command prompt and execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system.

C.quote: execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system.

I.quote: execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system.

A.quote: execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Request technical details and proof-of-concept from the reporter: exact CLI commands that are vulnerable, affected software version(s), and steps to reproduce the command-injection so PSIRT can validate and develop mitigations.

evidence_quotes.claim: Vulnerability affects product CLI and allows command execution
evidence_quotes.quote: Vulnerability in the CLI of Cisco Secure Email Gateway could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands.

evidence_quotes.claim: Cause is improper input validation in the CLI
evidence_quotes.quote: These vulnerability is due to improper input validation in the CLI.

evidence_quotes.claim: Attack technique: injecting OS commands into a legitimate command
evidence_quotes.quote: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by injecting operating system commands into a legitimate command.

evidence_quotes.claim: Impact: escape restricted prompt and execute arbitrary commands on the OS
evidence_quotes.quote: A successful exploit could allow the attacker to escape the restricted command prompt and execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system.
To successfully exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would need valid Administrator credentials.
